- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/22 (Mon) 16:25
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Shakshuka is a popular dish that originated in North Africa and has since spread to different parts of the world.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Shakshuka is a hearty, savory meal that can be enjoyed at any time of day.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Tools needed to make Shakshuka include a large pan (stainless or cast iron), sharp knife, cutting board, can opener, measuring spoons, wooden spoon, and garlic press (optional).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] To prepare the ingredients, chop one large onion or one and a half small ones, and mince four cloves of garlic.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Prepare the bell pepper by removing the ribs and seeds, and cutting it into small pieces.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Heat three tablespoons of olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Cook the onions and bell peppers for 10 to 12 minutes until the onions are translucent and starting to take on color.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Open a can of whole peeled tomatoes, drain some liquid, and add the tomatoes and minced garlic to the pan.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Create a small well in the mixture and crack an egg into it, repeating for as many eggs as desired.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Cover the pan with a lid and let the eggs cook for about 5-7 minutes until the whites are set and yolks are runny.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Garnish the Shakshuka with fresh herbs like parsley or cilantro, and serve with crusty bread or pita.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] To add more spice to Shakshuka, you can add jalapenos or other hot peppers.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] For a heartier dish, you can add cooked sausage or bacon.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Other vegetables like mushrooms or zucchini can be added for flavor and nutrition.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Cheese options include feta or Parmesan, which can be sprinkled on top before serving.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Shakshuka originated in North Africa and the name translates to "mixed it up" or "mixed."
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Shakshuka can be made without eggs, adjusting the cooking time accordingly.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Shakshuka can be stored in the fridge for up to three days.
